On Fri, Aug 14, 2026 at 10:02 AM dylan_brooks@redwood.ai wrote:
> Ben / Marissa — copying you to pull together artifacts for Bluecrest. Jamie asked for a runbook PDF and a real restore trace with per-stage timings.

Attaching: runbook_v3.pdf and restore_trace_20260810.log (sanitized) — both included in the attachments. Notes below.

Summary of the restore trace (sanitized):
- snapshot-restore-init: 00:00:00 -> 00:03:22 (3m22s)
- metadata-apply: 00:03:22 -> 00:04:07 (45s)
- model-load: 00:04:07 -> 00:12:14 (8m7s)
- kv-cache-warm (parallelized): 00:12:14 -> 00:16:50 (4m36s)
- health-checks & route-flip: 00:16:50 -> 00:17:30 (40s)

End-to-end measured restore in that rehearsal: 17m30s. That includes the KV warm procedure we ran in parallel with model load; the longest blocking step was model binary load on GPUs (8m7s).

RPO assumptions (as published):
- Primary region outage (regional failover to secondary): RPO = 0–15s for metadata and bookkeeping state; application-level state is reconstructed from S3 snapshots taken every 5s for critical streams.
- Single AZ failure (within primary region): RPO = near-zero due to cross-AZ replication.

Cache warming: the KV cache is warmed in parallel; our documented RTO assumes cache-warm is part of final steady-state but we treat a partial-warm state as acceptable for degraded throughput for up to 30 minutes while background warm continues. We explicitly document the warm progression in the runbook.

Attached runbook contains step-by-step, required roles, playbook commands, and rollback notes. The trace file is a raw sanitized log with timestamps per stage.

—Ben

Jamie — attaching the artifacts Ben prepared: runbook_v3.pdf (full restore playbook), restore_trace_20260810.log (sanitized trace), inference-arch-diagram.png, and our SOC2 summary. Key points for your audit: 

- The rehearsal on 2026-08-10 measured a full restore time of 17m30s including KV cache-warm. We consider the steady-state fully warm at ~20 minutes in that exercise.
- RPO for primary-regional failover is documented at <=15s for critical bookkeeping; for application-level streaming state we rely on frequent snapshots (5s cadence).
- Cache warm is run in parallel with model load; degraded throughput during warm is expected for up to 30 minutes and is documented as an operational tolerance in the runbook.
